figures.label: S19
figures.caption: Suppl. Fig. 19. Influence of halide species on Li-ion diffusion barriers for argyrodites with different anion disorder. Results are shown for Li6PS5X with X ∈Cl, Br, I, with (a) 0%, (b) 50%, and (c) 100% anion disorder. Consistency is observed across all argyrodites for the activation energy as a function of anion disorder. The bulk diffusion barriers decrease from 0% to 50% anion disorder and then increase from 50% to 100%. Grain boundaries hinder Li-ion diffusion at 50% anion disorder, while they enhance diffusion at 0%. The Li-ion diffusion barrier increases linearly with anion radius in anion-ordered bulk argyrodites, while exhibiting more complex behavior in other cases. Experimental values and uncertainties from electrochemical impedance spectroscopy measurements reported by Shotwell et al. [8] and Kraft et al. [44] are compared.

figures.label: S22
figures.caption: Suppl. Fig. 22. Impact of porosity on macroscopic conductivity of solid electrolytes at 300 K. Li6PS5Cl with 50% anion disorder is considered. The grain-size effect is estimated for a close-contact polycrystal using our multiscale modeling framework, while the porosity effect is applied as a shift on top of these close-contact results, based on theoretical models (ACS Appl. Energy Mater. [45] and Adv. Funct. Mater. [46]) and experimental measurements [46]. Accounting for porosity reduces the macroscopic conductivity by one to two orders of magnitude, bringing predictions for anion-disordered Li6PS5Cl closer to experimental observations.
